title: Docs: signed offline bundles (install + verify), troubleshooting, FAQ
author: Kira Thompson
description: Summary This PR adds the first customer-facing documentation for Redwood Private signed offline bundles (v1). It covers: (1) what the offline bundle is and what it contains, (2) how to verify bundle integrity/signature fully offline, (3) how to install using the offline bundle path, (4) what errors look like and how to troubleshoot, and (5) an FAQ focused on regulated / air-gapped questions (key custody, rotation, break-glass, and downgrade protections). Motivation Regulated customers are asking for a concrete, step-by-step workflow that doesn’t require outbound network access and that is consistent with installer behavior (fail-closed; explicit break-glass). This doc aligns with the installer CLI changes landing in redwood-private-installer (verify command + fail-closed verification before unpack/install + override flow). Scope / non-goals This doc describes Redwood-signed bundles only (v1). It does not cover customer-managed signing (explicitly called out in FAQ as not supported in v1). It does not document internal CI/KMS details beyond a high-level “how signatures are produced” note. Content outline added by this PR 1) Concept: Offline bundle + signature envelope (detached signature + manifest with digests). 2) Prereqs: air-gapped host requirements, required CLI/installer versions, and how to obtain Redwood public verification keys offline. 3) Verify: recommended workflow before transfer (online workstation) and after transfer (air-gapped environment), including command examples and expected output. 4) Install: using the installer with an offline bundle; verification behavior (what is verified, when it fails). 5) Troubleshooting: common failures (checksum mismatch after media transfer, signature mismatch, wrong keyset, stale/partial extraction, timestamp skew) and the diagnostic bundle to send to support. 6) FAQ: key rotation, revocation, verifying older bundles, break-glass policy, and how to validate SBOM/provenance references offline. Preview notes The doc assumes the installer provides: `redwood-private verify offline-bundle --bundle <path> --keys <path>` and that installation uses the same verification logic automatically prior to unpack/install. If the final subcommand differs, we should update examples prior to release. I kept the wording generic enough to map onto the final CLI with minimal edits. References Linear: ENG-3918 (primary), ENG-3914/3915 for CLI behavior. Security review requested per ENG-3915 (break-glass acknowledgement language).

notable_content_excerpt: Key excerpts added to the guide: Verification (recommended) 1) Before transferring media: run verification on a connected workstation to confirm you downloaded a complete bundle. 2) After transferring media: re-run verification on the air-gapped host. This detects corruption introduced during transfer (USB / offline repo sync). Command (example) `redwood-private verify offline-bundle --bundle /mnt/media/redwood-private-bundle-1.12.0.tgz --keys /mnt/media/redwood-public-keys/` Expected output (success) `OK signature=valid manifest=valid artifacts=valid` Fail-closed behavior If verification fails for any reason (signature invalid, manifest parse error, missing artifact, checksum mismatch), the installer will stop before unpacking or installing any components. Break-glass (emergency only) If you have explicit approval to proceed without a valid signature (for example, to recover a down environment while awaiting a re-issued bundle), you may use the break-glass flag. Doing so requires an interactive acknowledgement and emits an audit log entry indicating the override was used. Troubleshooting: checksum mismatch after transfer Symptoms: `artifact digest mismatch` or `missing blob` Errors typically indicate corruption during transfer or partial extraction. Actions: (a) re-copy the bundle from source, (b) prefer binary-safe transfer tools, (c) verify available disk space, (d) re-run verification from the original .tgz rather than an unpacked directory if possible. Diagnostics for support: run `redwood-private verify offline-bundle --bundle <path> --keys <path> --output diagnostics.json` and attach diagnostics.json plus the installer log.

Kira Thompson (author): Added to the intro + FAQ and emphasized “no outbound calls” in the Verify section. Also added a short “What data is sent?” note: none.

Marcus Lin (security review): Break-glass language needs to be stronger and should mirror policy: ‘emergency only’, ‘requires explicit acknowledgement’, and ‘creates an audit log entry’. Also please remove ‘recommended’ wording around fail-closed; it is required behavior.

Kira Thompson (author): Updated break-glass block to match policy language and changed fail-closed wording to be definitive. Added an include snippet so we can reuse the acknowledgement language consistently.

Markus Klein (SE): Troubleshooting section should include what to send to support and how to capture logs without leaking keys. Also: add a note about common pilot issue—digest mismatch after unpacking due to verifying the wrong path (directory vs tgz).

Kira Thompson (author): Added a ‘Collect diagnostics’ subsection + examples. Added guidance: don’t include private keys, include only public keys and installer logs. Added a callout about verifying from the bundle archive vs a partially-unpacked directory.

Fatima Noor (SE): Add guidance for air-gapped environments where `/tmp` is mounted noexec or small; installer extraction can fail in surprising ways. Also clarify disk space requirements and that verification requires reading the full bundle.

Kira Thompson (author): Added prerequisites: tmp space + alternate extraction dir via installer flag (if supported) with a note to consult installer help. Added a troubleshooting item for noexec/tmp size.

Kira Thompson (author): Updated expected output to be descriptive, not exact. Kept commands as examples with ‘may vary by version’ note.
